DIAGNOSIS READY: Wilson's disease (hepatolenticular degeneration).

Based on the combination of neuropsychiatric symptoms (hallucinations, irritability, memory loss), dysphagia, and the family history of premature suicide, this clinical picture strongly suggests Wilson's disease. The involuntary movements described as occurring at rest are likely tremors or dystonia associated with basal ganglia involvement. I will proceed with diagnostic testing to confirm copper metabolism abnormalities and assess liver involvement. REQUEST TEST: Serum ceruloplasmin, 24-hour urinary copper, and serum copper levels.
